sections.introduction:
Pippali Ghrita is a classical Ayurvedic medicated ghee formulation primarily indicated in Kshaya (emaciation, wasting disorders) and Kasa (chronic cough). It is a simple yet highly effective formulation prepared using Pippali (Piper longum — Long pepper), Guda (jaggery), Chaga Ghrita (goat ghee), and Chaga Kshira (goat milk). 
 This formulation is especially valued for its ability to enhance Agni (digestive fire), nourish depleted tissues (Dhatu Kshaya), and strengthen the respiratory system. Due to the presence of Pippali (Piper longum), it acts as a potent Rasayana (rejuvenator) for the lungs, improving both digestion and respiratory health simultaneously.

sections.ingredients:
Pippali Kalka (Piper longum — Long pepper paste) — 1/2 part 
 Guda (Jaggery — Saccharum officinarum product) — 1/2 part 
 Chaga Ghrita (Goat ghee) — 4 parts 
 Chaga Kshira (Goat milk) — 16 parts 

 Method Of Preparation 
 All the ingredients are taken in the specified proportions and mixed thoroughly in a clean vessel. The mixture is subjected to mild heating following classical Sneha Paka Vidhi (medicated ghee preparation process). It is cooked with continuous stirring until the liquid portion evaporates completely and only the medicated ghrita remains in the quantity of Chaga Ghrita (Goat ghee). After achieving proper Sneha Siddhi Lakshanas (signs of completion of medicated ghee formation), the preparation is filtered while warm and stored in clean, wide-mouthed glass containers. 
 Method Of Use 
 Internal Administration 
 Internal administration

sections.indications:
Kshaya (wasting disorders, including pulmonary weakness) 
 Kasa (chronic cough) 
 General debility and weakness 
 Poor digestion associated with chronic illness 

 Therapeutic Properties 
 Pippali (Piper longum) is the प्रमुख ingredient known for its Deepana (appetising), Pachana (digestive), and Rasayana (rejuvenating) properties. It enhances bioavailability (Yogavahi effect) and strengthens respiratory function. Guda (jaggery) provides nourishment and supports energy restoration, while also aiding in mild detoxification. Chaga Kshira (goat milk) is easily digestible and acts as a nourishing medium, especially beneficial in debilitated conditions. Chaga Ghrita (goat ghee) enhances tissue replenishment and acts as a carrier, ensuring deeper delivery of therapeutic components. Together, these ingredients help restore weakened Dhatus (body tissues), improve appetite, and reduce chronic cough.
sections.precautions:
Should be used under medical supervision 
 Use cautiously in individuals with high Pitta or hyperacidity 
 Avoid in acute febrile conditions with strong Ama presence 
 Monitor for digestive tolerance 

 Commentary 
 This formulation is described in classical texts such as Cakradatta (Rajayakshma Chikitsa 10:64) and Bhaishajya Ratnavali (Rajayakshma Chikitsa 14:237), indicating its significance in managing chronic respiratory and wasting disorders. 
 Conclusion 
 Pippali Ghrita is a simple yet powerful Ayurvedic formulation that effectively addresses Kshaya (wasting) and Kasa (cough) by improving digestion, nourishing tissues, and strengthening the respiratory system. Its balanced combination of Deepana (digestive) and Brimhana (strengthening) properties makes it particularly useful in chronic debilitating conditions. When used appropriately, it helps restore vitality, enhance immunity, and promote overall health.

Pippali Ghrita – Medicinal Properties, Ingredients, Indications, Dosage More 
 Introduction 
 Pippali Ghrita is a classical Ayurvedic medicated ghee formulation primarily indicated in Kshaya (emaciation, wasting disorders) and Kasa (chronic cough). It is a simple yet highly effective formulation prepared using Pippali (Piper longum — Long pepper), Guda (jaggery), Chaga Ghrita (goat ghee), and Chaga Kshira (goat milk). 
 This formulation is especially valued for its ability to enhance Agni (digestive fire), nourish depleted tissues (Dhatu Kshaya), and strengthen the respiratory system. Due to the presence of Pippali (Piper longum), it acts as a potent Rasayana (rejuvenator) for the lungs, improving both digestion and respiratory health simultaneously. 
 Reference Shloka 
 
पिप्पलीगुडसंसिद्ध छागक्षीरयुतं घृतम्। 
एतदग्निविवृध्यर्थम् सेव्यं वै क्षयकासिभिः ।। 
 
 Composition 
 Ingredients 
 
 Pippali Kalka (Piper longum — Long pepper paste) — 1/2 part 
 Guda (Jaggery — Saccharum officinarum product) — 1/2 part 
 Chaga Ghrita (Goat ghee) — 4 parts 
 Chaga Kshira (Goat milk) — 16 parts 
 
 Method Of Preparation 
 All the ingredients are taken in the specified proportions and mixed thoroughly in a clean vessel. The mixture is subjected to mild heating following classical Sneha Paka Vidhi (medicated ghee preparation process). It is cooked with continuous stirring until the liquid portion evaporates completely and only the medicated ghrita remains in the quantity of Chaga Ghrita (Goat ghee). After achieving proper Sneha Siddhi Lakshanas (signs of completion of medicated ghee formation), the preparation is filtered while warm and stored in clean, wide-mouthed glass containers. 
 Method Of Use 
 Internal Administration 
 Internal administration 
 Dose 
 10 gm twice daily 
 Anupana 
 Warm milk 
 Pharmacological Actions 
 
 Agnivardhana – enhances digestive fire 
 Rasayana – rejuvenates tissues 
 Kasahara – relieves cough 
 Shwasahara – supports respiratory function 
 Brimhana – nourishes and strengthens body tissues 
 Balya – improves strength and vitality 
 
 Indications 
 
 Kshaya (wasting disorders, including pulmonary weakness) 
 Kasa (chronic cough) 
 General debility and weakness 
 Poor digestion associated with chronic illness 
 
 Therapeutic Properties 
 Pippali (Piper longum) is the प्रमुख ingredient known for its Deepana (appetising), Pachana (digestive), and Rasayana (rejuvenating) properties. It enhances bioavailability (Yogavahi effect) and strengthens respiratory function. Guda (jaggery) provides nourishment and supports energy restoration, while also aiding in mild detoxification. Chaga Kshira (goat milk) is easily digestible and acts as a nourishing medium, especially beneficial in debilitated conditions. Chaga Ghrita (goat ghee) enhances tissue replenishment and acts as a carrier, ensuring deeper delivery of therapeutic components. Together, these ingredients help restore weakened Dhatus (body tissues), improve appetite, and reduce chronic cough. 
 Precautions 
 
 Should be used under medical supervision 
 Use cautiously in individuals with high Pitta or hyperacidity 
 Avoid in acute febrile conditions with strong Ama presence 
 Monitor for digestive tolerance 
 
 Commentary 
 This formulation is described in classical texts such as Cakradatta (Rajayakshma Chikitsa 10:64) and Bhaishajya Ratnavali (Rajayakshma Chikitsa 14:237), indicating its significance in managing chronic respiratory and wasting disorders. 
 Conclusion 
 Pippali Ghrita is a simple yet powerful Ayurvedic formulation that effectively addresses Kshaya (wasting) and Kasa (cough) by improving digestion, nourishing tissues, and strengthening the respiratory system. Its balanced combination of Deepana (digestive) and Brimhana (strengthening) properties makes it particularly useful in chronic debilitating conditions. When used appropriately, it helps restore vitality, enhance immunity, and promote overall health.
